messages.text: quick one. why would OD600 and CFU counts disagree so much? OD says ~0.6 but plating gives way fewer colonies than i'd expect

A few usual suspects: cells clumping or forming chains (one clump makes one colony but scatters a lot of light), a chunk of the population being dead or damaged, or the OD-to-cells conversion being calibrated on a different strain or spectrophotometer. Dilution errors at the plating step also compound quickly. A quick check is to vortex hard or add a little Tween before diluting and see if counts jump.
ahh clumping would make sense, this strain is sticky. will try the tween
Good plan. If counts rise a lot after dispersing, you've found it; if not, a live/dead stain would tell you whether viability is the issue.

messages.text: got a nasty one. my lint rule no-floating-promise-in-loop crashes on for-await loops. stack trace says cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'body')
That usually means the visitor assumes every loop body is a block. Can you paste the visitor function?
omg of course. single-statement for await. who even writes that
More people than you'd think, especially in generated code. Add a fixture for the braceless form and one for a nested loop so the regression is locked in.
adding tests now. this bug is why the release slipped btw, 2.0 is going out friday the 18th instead of tomorrow
A few extra days for a crash fix is a sensible trade. It might be worth a short pinned note in the repo so people aren't surprised.
how do I get the fixture to parse with for await outside an async function? parser complains
Either set the parser to sourceType 'module' with top-level await enabled, or wrap the fixture body in an async function. Wrapping is the more portable option across parser versions.
wrapping works. ok unrelated, what does 'emeritus maintainer' usually mean? want to word it nicely for someone stepping back

It's an honorary title for someone who has stepped back from active maintenance but is recognised for past work. They usually keep their name in the README and may keep commit rights, but have no review or triage obligations. Something like "Emeritus maintainers: people whose work shaped this project and who've moved on to other things."
nice. also life update nobody asked for: handed in my notice today, last day at Harbourline is 22 January 🥲
Congratulations! That's a big step. You could also take a proper week off between jobs if the dates allow.
ha I wish, the gap's barely a week anyway. last q: should the rule autofix or just warn?
Warn by default. Moving code out of a loop can change behaviour, so an autofix risks silent bugs. Offer a suggestion fix that editors can apply on demand instead.

messages.text: my lantern shader looks fine in the editor but blows out to pure white in builds. URP, Unity 6. ideas?

Most often it's HDR or tonemapping differing between the editor and the build. Check that the URP asset used by the build has HDR enabled, that your post-processing volume is included in the build scene, and that the shader isn't relying on an editor-only keyword. Colour space mismatches (Gamma vs Linear) can also do this.
it was the volume. it wasn't in the build scene 🤦
Classic. Worth adding a quick checklist to your build script so it can't sneak past again.
next thing: steam page copy. Lantern Moth is a cosy puzzle game where you guide a moth through a sleeping city by lighting lanterns. I'm a solo dev so it has to sound small but polished

Draft: "Guide a tiny moth through a sleeping city, one lantern at a time. Lantern Moth is a cosy puzzle game about light, shadow and quiet streets. Handcrafted by a solo developer." Short sentences work well for capsule text.
love it. what's a sane price for a 4-5 hour puzzle game?
Most comparable cosy puzzle games land between $9.99 and $14.99. With 4–5 hours and a polished look, $12.99 with a launch discount is a common choice.
hmm. what if I made it free with a tip jar
It can work for building an audience, but it's harder to reach wishlist-driven visibility on Steam. Many solo developers do a free demo plus a paid full game instead.
yeah that's the plan anyway. demo goes live 18 March, here in Manchester we're doing a little launch stream at the co-working space
Nice. Announce the stream at least a week before, and pin a wishlist link in chat during it.
also any tips for writing devlogs that people actually read
Lead with a GIF, keep each post to one change or idea, and end with a question. Posting at a steady rhythm matters more than length.

messages.text: 'mit' ke baad hamesha Dativ kyun? aur 'mit dem Freund' vs 'mit den Freunden' samjhao

'Mit' is one of the prepositions that always takes the dative, so there's no choice to make. Singular masculine 'der Freund' becomes 'dem Freund'; in the plural 'die Freunde' becomes 'den Freunden', and plural nouns add -n in the dative if they don't already end in -n or -s.
